samples.summary: Design doc overstates coverage: several TextEditor *keyboard* paths still write one store update per block, so the #1045 data-loss shape survives where the doc says it is fixed
samples.evidence: The new section states "`withUndoUnit()` is a `TextEditor` method, so it covers the keyboard and clipboard handlers and nothing else", and scopes the remaining gap to "`EditorAPI` toolbar operations" plus `replaceAll` (issue #1048). But keyboard handlers inside `TextEditor` itself still write unbatched per block: `handleTab` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2758 `forEachBlockInSelection` → `doc.setBlockType` per block), `handleIndent`/`handleOutdent` (:2803, :2824), and `applyStyleToSelection` → `Doc.applyInlineStyle`, which loops `store.applyStyle(blockId, …)` per block (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:438-440) — i.e. Cmd+B / Tab / Cmd+] over a select-all of 100 paragraphs is still ~100 Yorkie undo units against the 50-entry cap, the exact shape #1045 describes (oldest entries shifted off, edits unrecoverable). Neither `Cmd+B`-style inline styling nor the keyboard Tab path is listed in the deferred #1048 set, so a reader trusts a coverage claim that is not true and users keep losing edits on those actions.

samples.summary: `batch()` adopts a prior checkpoint via whole-document JSON value comparison, although the newly added `willWrite()` hook gives an exact O(1) signal for the same question
samples.evidence: `const adopted = top !== undefined && JSON.stringify(top) === beforeJson;` and the surrounding comment claims "there is no flag a mutation could reliably clear". This change introduces exactly such a hook: every mutator now calls `willWrite()` (memory.ts:210), so `snapshot()` could set a `checkpointClean` flag that `willWrite()` clears, making adoption exact and O(1) instead of a value-equality heuristic plus an extra full-document `JSON.stringify` on every batch (on top of the existing clone+stringify in `wroteNothing`). Value equality also conflates "nothing was written" with "writes cancelled out", which the code then relies on for the pop/adopt decision. Cost is confined to the codebase (extra per-keystroke stringify in MemDocStore hosts and a subtler invariant), so minor.

samples.summary: Three different "one undo unit" wrappers with three different snapshot orderings now coexist; the store absorbs the divergence instead of the callers converging
samples.evidence: `withNamedStyleChange` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1236) snapshots *inside* `doc.batch`, `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace` (view/link-run.ts:105) does the same, and the new `TextEditor.withUndoUnit` (text-editor.ts:3840) snapshots *outside* — which is what forces `MemDocStore.batch()` to grow the adoption path. The repo already has one batching seam (`DocStore.batch` / `Doc.batch`); a single shared helper that owns the snapshot ordering (and the render hold) would keep one answer to "how does an action become one undo unit" instead of three conventions plus a store-side reconciliation. No behavioural cost today, hence minor.

samples.summary: Unrelated bug fix bundled into the undo-unit change: the Cmd+Shift+V `disposed || pasting` re-validation plus two new tests
samples.evidence: `if (this.disposed || this.pasting) return;` added in `pastePlainTextFromClipboard`, with two new cases in packages/docs/test/view/large-paste-indicator.test.ts (`installPendingClipboard`, dispose/pasting races). This is an async-lifetime defect independent of the #1045 undo-granularity outcome — it would misbehave identically before the batching change. Reviewable on its own; folding it in widens the blast radius of a change whose stated outcome is undo granularity.

samples.summary: The "paint stays outside the batch" rule is enforced on only one of the three render seams
samples.evidence: The hold wrapper is installed on `this.requestRender` only. `requestCursorRender` and `requestRenderNoCursorScroll` are invoked directly at text-editor.ts:2981 and :2268 (`(this.requestCursorRender ?? this.requestRender)()`), bypassing `undoUnitDepth`. Neither call site sits inside a `withUndoUnit` today, so nothing breaks now, but the documented invariant is only structurally true for one seam — a future interior caller of the other two paints mid-batch silently.

samples.summary: Comment "Mirrors `MemSlidesStore.batch()`" is now stale — the two batch implementations have diverged
samples.evidence: `MemSlidesStore.batch()` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:1789-1803) still pushes a checkpoint unconditionally and clears the redo stack inside `batch()`, while `MemDocStore.batch()` now adopts checkpoints and defers redo invalidation to `willWrite()`. The retained "mirrors" claim points a reader at a store that no longer behaves the same way.

finding.summary: Design doc overstates coverage: several TextEditor *keyboard* paths still write one store update per block, so the #1045 data-loss shape survives where the doc says it is fixed
finding.evidence: The new section states "`withUndoUnit()` is a `TextEditor` method, so it covers the keyboard and clipboard handlers and nothing else", and scopes the remaining gap to "`EditorAPI` toolbar operations" plus `replaceAll` (issue #1048). But keyboard handlers inside `TextEditor` itself still write unbatched per block: `handleTab` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2758 `forEachBlockInSelection` → `doc.setBlockType` per block), `handleIndent`/`handleOutdent` (:2803, :2824), and `applyStyleToSelection` → `Doc.applyInlineStyle`, which loops `store.applyStyle(blockId, …)` per block (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:438-440) — i.e. Cmd+B / Tab / Cmd+] over a select-all of 100 paragraphs is still ~100 Yorkie undo units against the 50-entry cap, the exact shape #1045 describes (oldest entries shifted off, edits unrecoverable). Neither `Cmd+B`-style inline styling nor the keyboard Tab path is listed in the deferred #1048 set, so a reader trusts a coverage claim that is not true and users keep losing edits on those actions.

verdict.reason: Every factual claim in the finding checks out. docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md:313-321 states withUndoUnit "covers the keyboard and clipboard handlers and nothing else" and scopes the remaining unbatched-per-block gap to EditorAPI toolbar ops plus replaceAll, saying those lose writes "exactly as the keyboard paths did before #1045". But keyboard paths inside TextEditor still write unbatched per block: handleTab (text-editor.ts:2757-2769, bound at :1167-1169) and handleIndent/handleOutdent (:2799-2842, bound at :1353-1363) call saveSnapshot() then forEachBlockInSelection with per-block doc.setBlockType/applyBlockStyle and never open withUndoUnit; Cmd+B/I/U (:1232-1253) reaches toggleStyle -> applyStyleToSelection (:3561-3580) -> Doc.applyInlineStyle (model/document.ts:438-441), which issues one store.applyStyle per slice with no batch. The withUndoUnit call sites (:835, 1020, 1552, 2652, 2675, 2715, 3863, 4256, 5891) exclude all of these. The EditorAPI versions (view/editor.ts:3355-3358, 3516-3519, 3536-3558) are separate duplicate implementations, so the doc's deferred list does not cover the keyboard ones. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, reachable from ordinary keystrokes, unguarded, and design-doc accuracy is within the design-fit lane. Severity is arguable (the #1045 task goal, docs/tasks/active/20260907-docs-select-all-type-undo-todo.md:22-25, covers only selection-replacing edits, which could make this a minor doc-accuracy point), but arguable severity is not a named refutation ground, so the finding stays.
